dry: The Assembly approves a bill after a lengthy debate.
Lawmakers pass a bill after hours of discussion.
wahala: Senate approves budget after 11 hours of debate, 9 of them about lunch.
Assembly passes a bill after a debate in which the bill was mentioned twice.

dry: A federal agency opens a new office building.
Officials open a long-awaited federal facility.
wahala: A ministry cuts the ribbon on a building it started in the last administration.
The ribbon is cut on a federal project, and the contractor is thanked for his patience.

dry: A new committee is formed to review an earlier committee's report.
A government committee is set up to study a report.
wahala: A committee has been formed to review the report of the committee that reviewed the report.
Officials form a committee to study the report that recommended forming committees.

dry: A senior official's motorcade delays traffic in the capital.
Traffic in the capital halts for a ministerial convoy.
wahala: A motorcade slows traffic in Abuja, and the traffic is reported to have been informed.
The convoy of a minister reaches the meeting early. The meeting was not ready.

dry: The ministry hires consultants to review its own procedures.
Consultants are contracted to advise on a government plan.
wahala: A ministry hires consultants to advise on how to hire consultants.
Consultants submit a report recommending more consultants.

dry: A ministry releases a statement on ongoing efforts.
Officials issue a statement saying work continues.
wahala: A ministry issues a statement saying it has issued several statements.
Officials say efforts are ongoing. Efforts are asked to confirm.

dry: A planned national survey is delayed again.
Officials postpone the planned national census.
wahala: The census has been postponed to a date to be announced, and the date is also being reviewed.
A national survey is delayed so it can be properly surveyed.

dry: Long queues are reported at filling stations in the north.
Fuel queues stretch for hours in several cities.
wahala: Fuel queues in the North now have their own postcode.
The fuel queue in one city has opened a small market.

dry: Generator sales rise as power supply worsens.
Households buy more generators amid outages.
wahala: Generator sellers report their best quarter. The national grid reports it also had a quarter.
Households upgrade generators; the grid continues its sabbatical.

dry: The finance ministry reviews options to raise funds.
Officials search for ways to close the budget gap.
wahala: The finance ministry is said to be checking under the sofa cushions.
Officials search for money in budget lines they did not know existed.

dry: A federal agency inspects a major road project.
Officials tour a road under construction.
wahala: The Federal Roads Agency inspects a road and finds the hole it dug last year.
Officials tour a road project and agree that the road will be ready, eventually.

dry: Ministers attend a retreat on national development.
A government retreat is held to review progress.
wahala: Ministers attend a three-day retreat, which they describe as productive. The hotel agrees.
A government retreat reviews progress, mostly at the buffet.

dry: The government unveils a new reform plan.
A new reform plan is presented to the public.
wahala: A new reform plan is unveiled. Its predecessor, also a reform plan, is unavailable for comment.
The government presents a reform plan with a logo.

dry: A harvest report notes steady yields in several regions.
Agriculture officials report a stable harvest.
wahala: Agriculture officials say the harvest is fine. The farmers say they will confirm.
The harvest report is positive. The harvest has not yet been shown the report.

dry: Agencies defend their budget proposals before lawmakers.
Ministry heads appear before the Assembly on spending.
wahala: Agency heads defend their budgets before lawmakers and nobody asks what the budgets are.
Ministers appear before the Assembly and say that the figures are being confirmed.
